description: Agent Events: submit a published agenda with the event plan it was published from: the agenda with the event and each session or break with its id, the plan session it cites, its title, kind, start and end times, speaker and room; the plan with the event and each session or break with its id, title, kind, times, speaker and room. The signed report gives the agenda and the plan, each agenda entry paired with a plan entry by the session it cites and then by title, every plan session and break missing from the agenda named, each pair’s start and end times and speaker on each side, and every pair of entries that overlap in one room named, and counts them, and names a discrepant agenda: a plan session or break missing from the agenda, a session at another time or with another speaker than the plan, and two entries overlapping in one room; then an unplanned session or break, another title or room and another event name, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. Times stated on one side only, a speaker named on one side only, or a plan or agenda with no sessions leaves the agenda unverified. Times compare to the minute and read only as times of day, speakers read as people in either name order, and entries with no room stated read as one room. The schedule check reads one event’s published agenda against its plan: the Standing jobs rail tools wever_schedule-create, wever_schedule-list, wever_schedule-status and wever_schedule-cancel register, list, report on and cancel recurring jobs that run read-only Wever tools for a wallet on a cadence, keeping state and running other tools, while the schedule check keeps no state, registers nothing and runs nothing; and wever_deadline-check extracts every date and obligation from one document and builds a timeline, while the schedule check extracts nothing and builds no timeline, reading start and end times as fields across two documents. Verdict event_schedule_discrepant, event_schedule_partial, event_schedule_unverified or event_schedule_consistent. POST /api/event-schedule-check. Reads the event records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never books a venue, registers or invites anyone, sells or refunds a ticket, publishes an announcement, or judges whether an event should happen, was well run, or was worth attending, only whether its records agree with each other and with what was announced, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Events reads an organized event’s records for consistency between documents: an event brief, a published agenda, speaker confirmations, a registration list, a venue arrangement, a ticketing record, a public announcement and a post-event report, each against the requirements, plan, lineup, capacity and eligibility terms, brief, announced terms, schedule or records it should agree with. Beside it, the Standing jobs rail tools such as wever_schedule-create register, list, report on and cancel recurring jobs and keep state, and wever_meeting-brief states one meeting’s decisions and action items from its notes, while this family keeps no state, registers nothing, runs nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what was announced. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-events-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-events/.
